title: Real-Time Print Quality Prediction in FDM 3D Printing Using Gaussian Splatting Representations
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for predicting print quality in Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing using Gaussian splatting representations. We leverage the continuous spatial representation capabilities of 3D Gaussian splatting to model layer-by-layer deposition patterns and predict potential defects before they occur. Our method achieves 94.3% accuracy in predicting common printing failures such as warping, stringing, and layer adhesion issues. By training on a dataset of 5,000 print sequences captured through multi-view cameras, our model can identify problematic regions in real-time with sub-second latency. Experimental results demonstrate that our Gaussian splatting-based approach outperforms traditional CNN-based methods by 18% in early defect detection while requiring 40% less computational overhead.

title: Gaussian Splatting-Enhanced Predictive Modeling for Multi-Material SLA Printing
abstract: We introduce a predictive framework for multi-material stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing that employs Gaussian splatting to model complex resin interactions and curing dynamics. The continuous volumetric representation provided by Gaussian splatting enables precise prediction of interface behaviors between different photopolymer resins during the printing process. Our system integrates real-time spectroscopic data with Gaussian splat primitives to forecast curing anomalies and material incompatibilities. Testing across 15 different resin combinations shows our method reduces failed prints by 67% compared to rule-based prediction systems. The approach successfully predicts optimal exposure times and layer thicknesses for each material combination with mean absolute error of 0.08 seconds and 0.012mm respectively.

title: Thermal Field Prediction in Metal 3D Printing via Differentiable Gaussian Splatting
abstract: This work explores the application of differentiable Gaussian splatting for predicting thermal fields in Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) metal 3D printing. Traditional finite element methods for thermal simulation are computationally expensive, limiting their use in real-time control systems. Our Gaussian splatting-based neural representation learns to predict spatiotemporal temperature distributions from sparse sensor measurements and laser trajectory data. The model is trained on thermal imaging data from 200 print jobs across Ti-6Al-4V and AlSi10Mg alloys. Results show our method achieves temperature prediction accuracy within 15°C while running 250× faster than conventional FEM simulations. We demonstrate successful prediction of thermal gradients that correlate with residual stress patterns and microstructural defects.

title: Surface Roughness Prediction for Support Structure Removal Using Gaussian Splatting Analysis
abstract: We present a novel method for predicting post-removal surface quality of 3D printed parts using Gaussian splatting to analyze support structure contact regions. By representing both the part geometry and support interfaces as continuous Gaussian distributions, our system predicts surface roughness and required post-processing effort before printing begins. The model incorporates material properties, support contact angle, and density parameters to generate spatially-varying roughness predictions across the part surface. Validation studies on 300 printed parts show strong correlation (R² = 0.89) between predicted and measured Ra values. The system enables automated support placement optimization that reduces average post-processing time by 34% while maintaining mechanical requirements.

title: Geometric Accuracy Prediction in Large-Scale 3D Printing Through Adaptive Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Large-scale 3D printing systems face unique challenges in maintaining geometric accuracy due to material settling, thermal expansion, and mechanical compliance. This paper introduces an adaptive Gaussian splatting framework that predicts geometric deviations during large-format additive manufacturing. Our approach models the printed structure as a dynamic collection of Gaussian primitives that evolve based on physics-informed deformation models. The system continuously refines its predictions by incorporating real-time 3D scanning data captured during printing. Experiments on structures ranging from 0.5m to 3.2m in height demonstrate prediction accuracy of 0.8mm RMSE for final part dimensions. The method enables predictive path compensation that reduces dimensional errors by 62% compared to nominal toolpath planning.

title: Porosity Distribution Prediction in Polymer 3D Printing via Volumetric Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Understanding and predicting internal porosity is critical for ensuring mechanical integrity of 3D printed polymer parts. We develop a volumetric Gaussian splatting approach to predict three-dimensional porosity distributions based on printing parameters and material characteristics. Unlike surface-based methods, our technique represents the internal structure as a continuous density field encoded by Gaussian splat primitives. Training data comprises micro-CT scans of 450 specimens printed with varying infill patterns, speeds, and temperatures. The model successfully predicts void locations and sizes with 87% precision at 0.1mm³ resolution. Predicted porosity maps show strong agreement with experimental measurements (Dice coefficient = 0.83) and enable optimization of print parameters to achieve target density specifications.

title: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Predicting Print Bed Adhesion in FFF Manufacturing
abstract: First layer adhesion remains a primary cause of print failures in Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF). This research introduces a dynamic Gaussian splatting model that predicts bed adhesion quality by analyzing thermal and mechanical interactions between the extruded material and build platform. Our system models the first layer as evolving Gaussian distributions that capture local adhesion strength, thermal contact, and stress accumulation. By processing data from thermal cameras and force sensors during initial deposition, the model predicts which regions are likely to delaminate during subsequent layers. Testing across various materials (PLA, ABS, PETG, Nylon) and bed surfaces shows 91% accuracy in predicting adhesion failures before the 5th layer is complete. Early prediction enables adaptive interventions that reduce first-layer failure rates by 73%.

title: Multi-Scale Gaussian Splatting for Predicting Mechanical Properties in Lattice Structure 3D Printing
abstract: Predicting mechanical properties of 3D printed lattice structures requires capturing phenomena across multiple length scales. We propose a multi-scale Gaussian splatting framework that represents lattice geometry from individual struts (micro-scale) to overall structure (macro-scale) using hierarchical Gaussian representations. The model learns relationships between geometric features encoded in Gaussian parameters and mechanical properties through training on 800 compression tests of various lattice topologies. Our approach successfully predicts Young's modulus (R² = 0.92), yield strength (R² = 0.88), and failure modes of novel lattice configurations. The continuous representation enables gradient-based optimization of lattice designs to meet specific mechanical requirements while considering manufacturing constraints such as minimum feature size and achievable overhang angles.

title: Gaussian Splatting-Based Trajectory Prediction for Collision Avoidance in Multi-Nozzle 3D Printing
abstract: Multi-nozzle 3D printing systems offer increased throughput but face challenges in coordinating multiple toolheads to avoid collisions with printed geometry and other nozzles. This work presents a Gaussian splatting-based prediction system that models both the evolving printed geometry and nozzle trajectories as continuous Gaussian distributions. By representing uncertainty in actual vs. planned geometry due to material deformation and positioning errors, our method predicts potential collisions with probabilistic confidence bounds. The system generates alternative trajectories that maintain printing quality while avoiding detected conflicts. Implementation on a custom 4-nozzle FDM printer demonstrates 99.4% collision avoidance success rate across 150 test prints with complex geometries. The approach reduces total print time by 38% compared to conservative sequential printing strategies.

title: Residual Stress Prediction in Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing Using Neural Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Residual stresses in Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) lead to part distortion and can compromise structural integrity. This paper develops a neural Gaussian splatting approach for predicting three-dimensional residual stress distributions during WAAM processes. The method represents stress fields as learnable Gaussian primitives that evolve according to thermomechanical principles derived from observed deposition sequences. Training incorporates X-ray diffraction measurements and distortion data from 120 WAAM builds in steel and aluminum alloys. Our model predicts residual stress magnitudes within 45MPa mean absolute error and successfully forecasts distortion patterns that match experimental measurements with 0.6mm average deviation. The predictive capability enables pre-compensated path planning that reduces post-build distortion by 56% without requiring iterative build-measure-correct cycles.
